original: Steve Jobs is arguably one of the most successful CEOs ever. Apple's stock price has climbed from a little over $5 in December 1996 to more than $350 this month and it's hard to imagine Apple without him at the helm. But that wasn
sampled:
't always the case. Jobs' rise to the top of Apple was filled with multiple missteps, and Jobs himself seems to have had a hard time accepting failure as a part of the process.

"I'm the luckiest guy in the world," Jobs said in 2002, when he was already a legend at Apple. "I got to do what I wanted to do. I didn't have to do what I didn't want to do."

Jobs did well at Apple because he was obsessed with the product and never allowed himself to settle for mediocrity. But he failed in a lot of other parts of his life, too.
